changelog.change: Rewritten from the CV Bleeding/Reversal guide: major-bleeding definition, cause classification, cascade map, weight/INR-based 4F-PCC dosing (25-50 U/kg), DOAC table with the Dec 2025 US andexanet withdrawal, TEG/ROTEM interpretation, the bedside algorithm, and the pitfalls (4F-PCC thrombosis, vit K overshoot, reflex platelets in antiplatelet ICH).
Added unfractionated heparin (protamine) and LMWH rows; added the periprocedural bridging pointer.
Removed andexanet alfa as primary US recommendation following the Dec 22 2025 US market withdrawal; 4F-PCC now primary.

summary: Reversal once bleeding starts. Andexanet alfa (Andexxa) is no longer available in the US as of 2026-12-22 — 4F-PCC / aPCC is the only US reversal path for apixaban, rivaroxaban, and edoxaban.

body.text: Andexanet alfa was voluntarily withdrawn from the US market on 2026-12-22 (postmarketing thromboembolic signal). It remains available outside the US (EU conditional approval; marketed as Ondexxya in the UK / Japan). A non-US build should branch on region.

Major bleeding = fatal; OR a critical site (intracranial, intraspinal, pericardial, retroperitoneal, intra-articular, intramuscular with compartment syndrome); OR a Hgb drop ≥ 2 g/dL; OR ≥ 2 units transfused. It's this threshold, not the visible volume, that triggers reversal. Then ask: (1) haemodynamically unstable? (2) cause — drug, dilution, consumption, or structural? (3) specific antidote available, or only supportive / nonspecific reversal?

rows: Liver disease, hemophilia, vitamin K deficiency

body.text: Where the drugs hit: warfarin blocks synthesis of II/VII/IX/X · dabigatran = direct thrombin (IIa) inhibitor · rivaroxaban/apixaban/edoxaban = direct factor Xa inhibitors · heparin/LMWH potentiate antithrombin (IIa + Xa) · aspirin = irreversible platelet COX-1 · P2Y12 inhibitors block ADP-mediated platelet activation.

items: 4F-PCC, weight- and INR-based, 25-50 U/kg IV (fixed-dose protocols commonly ~1,500 IU). Preferred over 3F-PCC and FFP — corrects INR in minutes, lower volume.
PLUS vitamin K 5-10 mg IV over ~30 min — mandatory, not optional (factor VII in PCC has a ~6 h half-life; vitamin K sustains the reversal as PCC wears off).
Target INR < 1.5. Recheck INR q6-8h for 24-48 h; some patients need a repeat vitamin K dose.

rows: 5 g IV as two 2.5 g aliquots (repeat 5 g if bleeding persists with lab evidence of effect). Dabigatran is also dialyzable.
25-50 U/kg IV — now the default; no FDA-approved specific antidote remains on the US market

body.text: Activated charcoal if the last DOAC dose was within 2-4 h. PT/aPTT do not rule out a DOAC effect.

items: Unfractionated heparin: protamine sulfate 1 mg per 100 units given in the last 2-3 h (max ~50 mg; slow IV — hypotension / anaphylactoid reaction with rapid push).
LMWH (enoxaparin): protamine ~60% effective — 1 mg per 1 mg of enoxaparin if within 8 h.
Antiplatelet-associated life-threatening bleeding with a recent dose: platelet transfusion 1 unit; DDAVP 0.3 mcg/kg IV improves platelet adhesion (useful in uremia / aspirin effect).
Do NOT reflexively transfuse platelets in antiplatelet-associated ICH — the intuitive move, and the wrong one (PATCH trial: harm signal).

body.text: TEG / ROTEM — treat the deficit the trace shows
Typical adult TEG: R 5-10 min, K 1-3 min, angle 53-72°, MA 50-70 mm, LY30 < 3% (use your lab's range).

items: 1. Unstable? → activate massive transfusion, call for help.
2. Identify the agent and last-dose time; choose a specific antidote if one is still available.
3. Send TEG/ROTEM + PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, platelets.
4. Treat the specific deficit the trace shows — not a blind shotgun of products.
5. Reassess the trace and labs after each intervention.

body.text: Pitfalls: 4F-PCC carries a real prothrombotic signal — restart anticoagulation as soon as safely possible (this postmarketing signal is what pulled andexanet from the US market). Vitamin K > 10 mg can make re-warfarinization difficult for days. Protamine → hypotension / anaphylactoid reaction, infuse slowly. The old andexanet 'interferes with heparin monitoring' warning no longer applies in the US — remove it from order sets.

Weigh the thrombotic risk of the underlying condition against the bleeding risk of the planned procedure — pulls conceptually from Caprini / Padua / IMPROVE in Calculators. For neuraxial and deep blocks, the timing thresholds are stricter and different — see the neuraxial-anticoagulation module.
